title: Dormant Cards, Stopped Cards and the Security of the Allowance
content:
A card that has gone the tier's dormancy period without a settled purchase is flagged dormant, and the member is written to and asked whether they still want it. The clauses below govern a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card that is idle, lost or under enquiry.

**Dormancy costs the member nothing.** Dormancy stops nothing the member has already earned: the balance stays on the card subject to the ordinary expiry rules, and nothing is charged for bringing the card back into use.

**Coming back into use.** A dormant card is brought back into use on the member's word alone, because only they can say they still want it, and the loads for later periods carry on as before.

**A card reported lost or stolen.** A card the member reports lost or stolen is stopped at once, on their statement, because the money on it is theirs to protect and delay costs them.

**A card the plan stops itself.** A card the plan itself stops for suspected misuse stays stopped for no longer than the tier's suspension days while the transactions are looked into, and the member is told on the day it is stopped what is happening and when they will hear.

**Release.** A stopped card is released only once the enquiry ends or a replacement card is activated, and the balance is never lost while the card is stopped.

**What the dormancy clock runs from.** Dormancy is measured from the last settled purchase, never from the last authorisation or the last load, so a card that only ever received loads becomes dormant on time. The days since the last settled purchase are read from the card's own entries.

**A point of judgement.** A card that has taken four scheduled loads and made no settled purchase at all is measured from the last settled purchase like any other: having none, it reaches its tier's dormancy period and is flagged dormant, and the loads it received do not put the clock back.
